title: 2021 Fall AMC 12B Problem 13
statement: Let \(c = \dfrac{2\pi}{11}.\) What is the value of \[\small \dfrac{\sin 3c \cdot \sin 6c \cdot \sin 9c \cdot \sin 12c \cdot \sin 15c}{\sin c \cdot \sin 2c \cdot \sin 3c \cdot \sin 4c \cdot \sin 5c}?\]

solutions.text:
Write each angle as \(kc = \dfrac{2\pi k}{11}.\) Reducing modulo \(2\pi,\) \(\sin 12c = \sin c\) and \(\sin 15c = \sin 4c.\)

So the numerator is \(\sin 3c \cdot \sin 6c \cdot \sin 9c\) \(\cdot \sin c \cdot \sin 4c.\) Cancelling the common factors \(\sin c,\) \(\sin 3c,\) \(\sin 4c\) leaves \(\dfrac{\sin 6c \cdot \sin 9c}{\sin 2c \cdot \sin 5c}.\)

Now \(\sin 9c = \sin\left(2\pi - 2c\right) = -\sin 2c\) and \(\sin 6c = \sin\left(2\pi - 5c\right) = -\sin 5c,\) so the ratio equals \(\dfrac{(-\sin 5c)(-\sin 2c)}{\sin 2c \cdot \sin 5c} = 1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Each angle is a multiple of \(\dfrac{2\pi}{11}\); reduce the numerator angles modulo \(2\pi\)
Use \(\sin(2\pi - x) = -\sin x\) to relate leftover numerator factors to denominator factors
